name: Cockroach Labs, Inc.
origin_detail: Founded in New York by ex-Google engineers Spencer Kimball and Peter Mattis (Google File System team; earlier co-authors of GIMP at UC Berkeley) and Ben Darnell (Google Reader). CockroachDB began as an open-source project inspired by Google Spanner; after VC interest the company was incorporated in February 2015. CockroachDB 1.0 shipped May 2017.
openness_notes: CockroachDB started as Apache-2.0 open source; enterprise features later went under the source-available Cockroach Community License (open core, 2). From v19.2 (2019) the core moved to BSL 1.1 (converting to Apache-2.0 after three years). From v24.3 (2024-11-18) the free Core edition was retired and all self-hosted use falls under a single proprietary 'CockroachDB Software License', with free use only for individuals, students, academics and firms under $10M revenue. Source remains visible, so level 1 (arguably near 0).

license_history.note: Open-source project before and at incorporation.

license_history.license: BSL 1.1 (core, from v19.2; converts to Apache-2.0 after 3 years) + Cockroach Community License (enterprise features)
license_history.note: v19.1.x stayed Apache-2.0; only restriction was offering CockroachDB as a service without an enterprise licence.

license_history.license: CockroachDB Software License (single Enterprise licence; free tier for <$10M revenue)
license_history.note: Announced 2024-08-15, effective with v24.3 on 2024-11-18; self-hosted only, cloud unchanged; government entities do not qualify for free use.

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Framed as protection against AWS-style hosted resale. No significant community fork; Apache-2.0 competitors (YugabyteDB, TiDB) used it in marketing.

relicensing_events.to: CockroachDB Software License (single proprietary enterprise licence)
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Ended the free Core edition to make larger companies pay; covered by The Register as 'abandoning open core'. No fork reported.

risk_events: 2024-11-18: Free Core edition retired; single proprietary licence
2026-09-02: Reported reduction of ~50 staff (~6.8%), listed as an unconfirmed rumor on Blind's tracker
No IPO or new priced round since the 2021 $5B valuation (no S-1 as of mid-2026)
robustness: Single-vendor, VC-backed, private since 2015; no foundation and no fork, so customers depend on Cockroach Labs. Funding of $633M gives runway, but the $5B valuation is from the 2021 peak and has not been re-priced publicly. PostgreSQL wire compatibility gives customers some portability.
openness_effect_assessment: Apache licensing and the Spanner pedigree drew early developer interest and large venture rounds (to a $5B valuation in 2021). The company then closed in two steps, BSL in 2019 and a single proprietary licence in 2024, without provoking a fork, likely because its user base was smaller and hyperscalers already had their own distributed SQL services. Closing is aimed at monetizing large self-hosted users; there is no public evidence yet whether it raised revenue.
key_takeaway: Cockroach Labs shows that a database company can move from Apache to nearly proprietary with little community backlash when the project lacks a large independent contributor base or a hyperscaler with motive to fork. The cost is that it now competes as a proprietary vendor against Apache-licensed rivals (YugabyteDB, TiDB) and Postgres itself, with no public exit and a valuation last set at the 2021 peak.
